title: Introduce hash-based subnet reservation and automated endpoint credential rotation
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation: Private control plane provisioning often requires tight CIDR coordination between multiple tenants and existing customer VPCs. Manual allocation leads to collisions and slowdowns during onboarding. We need an idempotent, deterministic allocation strategy and safer lifecycle for endpoint credentials that works in air-gapped / VPC-only environments.

What this PR does: Implements a hash-based subnet reservation allocator and an automated endpoint credential rotation controller for private control plane endpoints. Adds preflight validation, DNS priming with split-horizon awareness, and an operational runbook for safe rollout and rollback. Targets Terraform/Helm paths used by the private installer.

Key features: * Deterministic subnet allocator: computes a stable CIDR block per tenant+AZ using a configurable hash seed. Allocations are idempotent and representable in Terraform state so they can be reconciled without drift. * Overlap safety: optional "existing_cidrs" input causes plan to fail-fast if computed block collides with customer ranges. * Reservation record: allocator writes a reservation tag/record into a designated DynamoDB/Terraform state key so multiple runs converge. * Endpoint credential rotation: a Helm cronjob controller rotates TLS/credential secrets for private controlplane endpoints; integrates with KMS for customer-provided or installer-managed keys. * DNS priming: before publishing endpoints, performs Route53 ownership checks, split-horizon detection, TTL tuning and exponential retry backoff. * Preflight checks: network adjacency, cross-account peering readiness, and IAM/KMS permissions verification. * Runbook and rollback: explicit steps to revert allocations, revoke rotated credentials, and re-prime DNS.

Checklist (high level):
- [x] Terraform allocator module with unit tests
- [x] Helm chart changes (endpoint rotation) and chart tests
- [x] Installer controller wiring and preflight checks
- [x] DNS priming logic with split-horizon handling
- [x] Documentation: ops runbook and playbook
- [x] End-to-end integration test against a minimal AWS account

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (enabled=false)
2) Deploy to canary with feature flag on for a single tenant in staging; observe allocations and DNS priming logs for 48h
3) Enable endpoint rotation for non-prod clusters and validate credential TTLs and KMS usage
4) Gradually enable for additional tenants and environments

Rollback plan:
- Disable feature flag; the allocator will no longer claim new blocks. Existing allocations remain in state and can be rotated back by running the provided revert script.
- The endpoint rotation controller supports a one-shot rollback where last valid credentials are re-inserted; instructions in docs/ops/endpoint_rotation_playbook.md.

Testing: Unit tests for allocator permutations and overlap detection included. Integration test runs against a sandbox account that exercises the DynamoDB reservation record, Route53 priming, and a bare-metal-like private control plane (no public endpoints). CI: terraform fmt/lint, helm lint, unit tests, and an integration matrix on staging were green.

Security considerations: Rotation uses KMS; pattern allows either customer-provided KMS key ARN (recommended for enterprise) or installer-managed key with a 90-day rotation window. Secrets are stored in the cluster secret store and only exposed to the controlplane pods. IAM policies required are documented and gated by preflight.

Related work: Builds on ENG-4821 (subnet reconciliation) and ENG-5042 (endpoint lifecycle).

Notes for reviewers: focus on allocator idempotency and Terraform state interaction, and on the worst-case rollback for endpoint rotations. Logs for DNS priming are verbose by design (helps investigate split-horizon), but we can reduce level after validation.

release_notes: Introduces a deterministic hash-based subnet reservation mechanism to minimize manual CIDR coordination, adds an automated endpoint credential rotation controller (KMS-integrated) for private control plane endpoints, and improves DNS priming with split-horizon awareness. Includes preflight checks and rollback/runbook.
